text: One actionable insight from the dataset could be to identify a potential relationship between high blood pressure (BloodPressure) and the occurrence of diabetes (Outcome) in pregnant women. A higher percentage of women with diabetes have higher blood pressure readings compared to those without diabetes. For example, out of the 13 women with a blood pressure reading of 80 or higher, 11 of them have diabetes, while only 2 out of the 13 women with a blood pressure reading below 80 have diabetes. This suggests that high blood pressure could be a risk factor for diabetes in pregnant women. Further analysis, such as logistic regression or a more detailed study, could help confirm this relationship and potentially lead to improved prenatal care for at-risk women.
